problem: Find the point(s) of the intersection of the sphere $(x-2)^{2}+(y+6)^{2}+{z}^{2}=121$ and the line $\frac{x-2}{2}=\frac{y+6}{6}=\frac{z+11}{2}.$
worked_solution:
First, we write the equation of our line in parametric form:

$$
\frac{x-2}{2}=\frac{y+6}{6}=\frac{z+11}{2}=t\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}x=2t+2 \\ y=6t-6 \\ z=2t-11,\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Substituting the above expressions for $x$, $y$, and $z$ into the equation of the sphere, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-2)^{2}+(y+6)^{2}+{z}^{2} & =121 \\ ((2t+2)-2)^{2}+((6t-6)+6)^{2}+(2t-11)^{2} & =121 \\ (2t)^{2}+(6t)^{2}+(2t-11)^{2} & =121 \\ 4{t}^{2}+36{t}^{2}+(4{t}^{2}-44t+121) & =121 \\ 44{t}^{2}-44t+121 & =121 \\ 44{t}^{2}-44t & =0 \\ t(t-1) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we get the solutions $t=0$ and $t=1.$ 

Now, we substitute our solutions back into the equations of the line.

- For $t=0$, we have

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=2(0)+2=2 \\ y=6(0)-6=-6 \\ z=2(0)-11=-11,\end{aligned}
$$

so the first point is $(2,-6,-11).$

- For $t=1$, we have

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=2(1)+2=4 \\ y=6(1)-6=0 \\ z=2(1)-11=-9,\end{aligned}
$$

so the second point is $(4,0,-9).$

Therefore, the points of intersection are $(2,-6,-11)$ and $(4,0,-9).$
